newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes $2.50 lower on weaker crude.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes $2.50 lower on weaker crude.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures settled $2.50 lower on Thursday, dragged down by weaker crude and a seasonal decline in the heating oil market, traders said.

"The fall started off with crude and weakness from the APIs, but after recovering from the lows it continued in a weak range. The contract hit perfect resistance at $178 a tonne and created a buying signal in our system," a trader said.
"It's also part of the seasonal shift to distillate weakness and gasoline strength."
March gas oil settled at $173.50 a tonne, $1.75 above the day's low, after opening at $176 and touching a high of $178.
IPE April Brent crude futures were trading 34 cents lower at $20.29 a barrel at 1755 GMT, after recovering from two 20 cent slides in light choppy midafternoon trade to $20.17 and then $20.11.

"We were just following the TI (West Texas Intermediate) down," a trader said. "New York fell and triggered some stops. Some locals who were short over there (in New York) joined in the selling over here."

NYMEX crude was down 54 cents at $22.25 on bearish views of ample supply after stock data showed the first year-on-year surplus in three months. API stock figures released late on Wednesday showed U.S. crude oil inventories rose by 3.12 million barrels last week.

London traders said April Brent had triggered rapid selling after breaking key support at $20.32. Some said Brent would have to regain that level to stand a chance of maintaining a $20.30-20.50 range.
Support was put at $20.10 followed by $20.00.
